prompt:
I need the front end for Fundcycle. A grant-season planning tool that small nonprofits subscribe to for arranging funder deadlines, drafting work and reports around the availability of the few staff who do it all.

Who's using it: Renée Castillo, development director at Clearwater Watershed Education, an eight-person nonprofit that runs stream science field trips for middle schools. She's the only full-time fundraiser. Drafting, budgets and sign-offs are spread across the executive director, the finance manager and two program leads who write the program sections.

What they're doing right now: This morning the Hollis Family Foundation emailed that its letter of inquiry deadline has moved up from Jan 30 to Jan 9. That lands in the same week as the finance manager's year-end audit prep and right after the executive director's holiday leave (Dec 22 – Jan 4). Renée has to rearrange the next ten weeks. She has to decide who drafts which sections and when, which smaller applications can slip to their regular deadlines, and whether the ED can sign the Hollis letter before she leaves. She also needs to propose a revised plan to the team before Monday's staff meeting, where people will confirm or push back on their assignments.

What's in the system at this point: 23 funder opportunities for FY27 with deadlines from Dec 2026 to Jun 2027 and asks from $5,000 to $120,000, each with a status (researching, invited, drafting, submitted, awarded, declined). Six of them have interim or final reports due. Each opportunity breaks into tasks: narrative, budget, evaluation section, board letter, attachments, ED signature. Each task has an owner and an estimated effort of 1–12 hours. Staff availability: ED on leave Dec 22 – Jan 4, finance manager at 25% capacity Jan 5–16 for the audit, program lead Tomás out Dec 15–19 for field training, office closed Dec 24–Jan 1. A board meeting on Jan 14 is needed for the resolution two state grants require. Last year's submission dates are kept for comparison.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
